audit_status.source_base: Hebrew 1 Kings / Melakhim Aleph chapter 1, first-pass draft aligned to public-domain verse structure; formal witness audit remains required.
audit_status.review_note: Reviewed for elder care, Abishag's agency and consent, succession secrecy, Bathsheba's survival risk, royal anointing, sanctuary, and threatened execution.

verses.restored: King David was old, advanced in days. They covered him with garments, but he could not become warm.

familiar.text: Now king David was old and stricken in years; and they covered him with clothes, but he gat no heat.

modern.text: Now King David was old and well along in years, and though they covered him with blankets, he could not keep warm.

original.text: וְהַמֶּ֤לֶךְ דָּוִד֙ זָקֵ֔ן בָּ֖א בַּיָּמִ֑ים וַיְכַסֻּ֨הוּ֙ בַּבְּגָדִ֔ים וְלֹ֥א יִחַ֖ם לֽוֹ

verses.restored: His servants said, Let them seek for my lord the king a young virgin. Let her stand before the king, care for him, and lie in your embrace, so my lord the king may become warm.

familiar.text: Wherefore his servants said unto him, Let there be sought for my lord the king a young virgin: and let her stand before the king, and let her cherish him, and let her lie in thy bosom, that my lord the king may get heat.

modern.text: So his servants said to him, “Let us search for a young virgin for our lord the king, to attend to him and care for him and lie by his side to keep him warm.”

original.text: וַיֹּ֧אמְרוּ ל֣וֹ עֲבָדָ֗יו יְבַקְשׁ֞וּ לַאדֹנִ֤י הַמֶּ֨לֶךְ֙ נַעֲרָ֣ה בְתוּלָ֔ה וְעָֽמְדָה֙ לִפְנֵ֣י הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ וּתְהִי ל֖וֹ סֹכֶ֑נֶת וְשָׁכְבָ֣ה בְחֵיקֶ֔ךָ וְחַ֖ם לַאדֹנִ֥י הַמֶּֽלֶךְ

verses.restored: They sought a beautiful young woman throughout all territory of Israel and found Abishag the Shunammite, and brought her to the king.

familiar.text: So they sought for a fair damsel throughout all the coasts of Israel, and found Abishag a Shunammite, and brought her to the king.

modern.text: Then they searched throughout Israel for a beautiful girl, and they found Abishag the Shunammite and brought her to the king.

original.text: וַיְבַקְשׁוּ֙ נַעֲרָ֣ה יָפָ֔ה בְּכֹ֖ל גְּב֣וּל יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וַֽיִּמְצְא֗וּ אֶת אֲבִישַׁג֙ הַשּׁ֣וּנַמִּ֔ית וַיָּבִ֥אוּ אֹתָ֖הּ לַמֶּֽלֶךְ

verses.restored: The young woman was exceedingly beautiful. She cared for the king and served him, but the king did not know her sexually.

familiar.text: And the damsel was very fair, and cherished the king, and ministered to him: but the king knew her not.

modern.text: The girl was unsurpassed in beauty; she cared for the king and served him, but he had no relations with her. Adonijah Usurps the Kingdom

original.text: וְהַֽנַּעֲרָ֖ה יָפָ֣ה עַד מְאֹ֑ד וַתְּהִ֨י לַמֶּ֤לֶךְ סֹכֶ֨נֶת֙ וַתְּשָׁ֣רְתֵ֔הוּ וְהַמֶּ֖לֶךְ לֹ֥א יְדָעָֽהּ

verses.restored: Adonijah son of Haggith exalted himself, saying, I will be king. He prepared chariots, riders, and fifty men running before him.

familiar.text: Then Adonijah the son of Haggith exalted himself, saying, I will be king: and he prepared him chariots and horsemen, and fifty men to run before him.

modern.text: At that time Adonijah, David’s son by Haggith, began to exalt himself, saying, “I will be king!” And he acquired chariots and horsemen and fifty men to run ahead of him.

original.text: וַאֲדֹנִיָּ֧ה בֶן חַגִּ֛ית מִתְנַשֵּׂ֥א לֵאמֹ֖ר אֲנִ֣י אֶמְלֹ֑ךְ וַיַּ֣עַשׂ ל֗וֹ רֶ֚כֶב וּפָ֣רָשִׁ֔ים וַחֲמִשִּׁ֥ים אִ֖ישׁ רָצִ֥ים לְפָנָֽיו

verses.restored: His father had never grieved/challenged him by saying, Why have you done this? He also was very good in appearance, and his mother bore him after Absalom.

familiar.text: And his father had not displeased him at any time in saying, Why hast thou done so? and he also was a very goodly man; and his mother bare him after Absalom.

modern.text: (His father had never once reprimanded him by saying, “Why do you act this way?” Adonijah was also very handsome, born next after Absalom.)

original.text: וְלֹֽא עֲצָב֨וֹ אָבִ֤יו מִיָּמָיו֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר מַדּ֖וּעַ כָּ֣כָה עָשִׂ֑יתָ וְגַם ה֤וּא טֽוֹב תֹּ֨אַר֙ מְאֹ֔ד וְאֹת֥וֹ יָלְדָ֖ה אַחֲרֵ֥י אַבְשָׁלֽוֹם

verses.restored: He conferred with Joab son of Zeruiah and Abiathar the priest, and they supported Adonijah.

familiar.text: And he conferred with Joab the son of Zeruiah, and with Abiathar the priest: and they following Adonijah helped him.

modern.text: So Adonijah conferred with Joab son of Zeruiah and with Abiathar the priest, who supported him.

original.text: וַיִּהְי֣וּ דְבָרָ֔יו עִ֚ם יוֹאָ֣ב בֶּן צְרוּיָ֔ה וְעִ֖ם אֶבְיָתָ֣ר הַכֹּהֵ֑ן וַֽיַּעְזְר֔וּ אַחֲרֵ֖י אֲדֹנִיָּֽה

verses.restored: But Zadok the priest, Benaiah son of Jehoiada, Nathan the prophet, Shimei, Rei, and David's warriors were not with Adonijah.

familiar.text: But Zadok the priest, and Benaiah the son of Jehoiada, and Nathan the prophet, and Shimei, and Rei, and the mighty men which belonged to David, were not with Adonijah.

modern.text: But Zadok the priest, Benaiah son of Jehoiada, Nathan the prophet, Shimei, Rei, and David’s mighty men would not join Adonijah.

original.text: וְצָד֣וֹק הַ֠כֹּהֵן וּבְנָיָ֨הוּ בֶן יְהוֹיָדָ֜ע וְנָתָ֤ן הַנָּבִיא֙ וְשִׁמְעִ֣י וְרֵעִ֔י וְהַגִּבּוֹרִ֖ים אֲשֶׁ֣ר לְדָוִ֑ד לֹ֥א הָי֖וּ עִם אֲדֹנִיָּֽהוּ

verses.restored: Adonijah sacrificed sheep, cattle, and fattened animals by stone of Zoheleth beside En-rogel. He invited all his brothers, the king's sons, and all men of Judah serving the king.

familiar.text: And Adonijah slew sheep and oxen and fat cattle by the stone of Zoheleth, which is by Enrogel, and called all his brethren the king’s sons, and all the men of Judah the king’s servants:

modern.text: And Adonijah sacrificed sheep, oxen, and fattened calves near the stone of Zoheleth, which is next to En-rogel. He invited all his royal brothers and all the men of Judah who were servants of the king.

original.text: וַיִּזְבַּ֣ח אֲדֹנִיָּ֗הוּ צֹ֤אן וּבָקָר֙ וּמְרִ֔יא עִ֚ם אֶ֣בֶן הַזֹּחֶ֔לֶת אֲשֶׁר אֵ֖צֶל עֵ֣ין רֹגֵ֑ל וַיִּקְרָ֗א אֶת כָּל אֶחָיו֙ בְּנֵ֣י הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ וּלְכָל אַנְשֵׁ֥י יְהוּדָ֖ה עַבְדֵ֥י הַמֶּֽלֶךְ

verses.restored: But he did not invite Nathan the prophet, Benaiah, the warriors, or Solomon his brother.

familiar.text: But Nathan the prophet, and Benaiah, and the mighty men, and Solomon his brother, he called not.

modern.text: But he did not invite Nathan the prophet, Benaiah, the mighty men, or his brother Solomon. Nathan and Bathsheba before David

original.text: וְֽאֶת נָתָן֩ הַנָּבִ֨יא וּבְנָיָ֜הוּ וְאֶת הַגִּבּוֹרִ֛ים וְאֶת שְׁלֹמֹ֥ה אָחִ֖יו לֹ֥א קָרָֽא

verses.restored: Nathan spoke to Bathsheba, mother of Solomon: Have you not heard that Adonijah son of Haggith has become king, while David our lord does not know?

familiar.text: Wherefore Nathan spake unto Bathsheba the mother of Solomon, saying, Hast thou not heard that Adonijah the son of Haggith doth reign, and David our lord knoweth it not?

modern.text: Then Nathan said to Bathsheba the mother of Solomon, “Have you not heard that Adonijah son of Haggith has become king, and our lord David does not know it?

original.text: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר נָתָ֗ן אֶל בַּת שֶׁ֤בַע אֵם שְׁלֹמֹה֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר הֲל֣וֹא שָׁמַ֔עַתְּ כִּ֥י מָלַ֖ךְ אֲדֹנִיָּ֣הוּ בֶן חַגִּ֑ית וַאֲדֹנֵ֥ינוּ דָוִ֖ד לֹ֥א יָדָֽע

verses.restored: Now come, please let me counsel you, so you may rescue your life and life of your son Solomon.

familiar.text: Now therefore come, let me, I pray thee, give thee counsel, that thou mayest save thine own life, and the life of thy son Solomon.

modern.text: Now please, come and let me advise you. Save your own life and the life of your son Solomon.

original.text: וְעַתָּ֕ה לְכִ֛י אִיעָצֵ֥ךְ נָ֖א עֵצָ֑ה וּמַלְּטִי֙ אֶת נַפְשֵׁ֔ךְ וְאֶת נֶ֥פֶשׁ בְּנֵ֖ךְ שְׁלֹמֹֽה

verses.restored: Go to King David and say: Did you not swear to your maidservant, Solomon your son shall reign after me and sit upon my throne? Why then has Adonijah become king?

familiar.text: Go and get thee in unto king David, and say unto him, Didst not thou, my lord, O king, swear unto thine handmaid, saying, Assuredly Solomon thy son shall reign after me, and he shall sit upon my throne? why then doth Adonijah reign?

modern.text: Go at once to King David and say, ‘My lord the king, did you not swear to your maidservant, “Surely your son Solomon will reign after me, and he will sit on my throne”? Why then has Adonijah become king?’

original.text: לְכִ֞י וּבֹ֣אִי אֶל הַמֶּ֣לֶךְ דָּוִ֗ד וְאָמַ֤רְתְּ אֵלָיו֙ הֲלֹֽא אַתָּ֞ה אֲדֹנִ֣י הַמֶּ֗לֶךְ נִשְׁבַּ֤עְתָּ לַאֲמָֽתְךָ֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר כִּֽי שְׁלֹמֹ֤ה בְנֵךְ֙ יִמְלֹ֣ךְ אַחֲרַ֔י וְה֖וּא יֵשֵׁ֣ב עַל כִּסְאִ֑י וּמַדּ֖וּעַ מָלַ֥ךְ אֲדֹנִיָֽהוּ

verses.restored: Look, while you are still speaking there with the king, I will come after you and confirm your words.

familiar.text: Behold, while thou yet talkest there with the king, I also will come in after thee, and confirm thy words.

modern.text: Then, while you are still there speaking with the king, I will come in after you and confirm your words.”

original.text: הִנֵּ֗ה עוֹדָ֛ךְ מְדַבֶּ֥רֶת שָׁ֖ם עִם הַמֶּ֑לֶךְ וַאֲנִי֙ אָב֣וֹא אַחֲרַ֔יִךְ וּמִלֵּאתִ֖י אֶת דְּבָרָֽיִךְ

verses.restored: Bathsheba went to the king in the chamber. The king was very old, and Abishag the Shunammite was serving the king.

familiar.text: And Bathsheba went in unto the king into the chamber: and the king was very old; and Abishag the Shunammite ministered unto the king.

modern.text: So Bathsheba went to see the king in his bedroom. Since the king was very old, Abishag the Shunammite was serving him.

original.text: וַתָּבֹ֨א בַת שֶׁ֤בֶע אֶל הַמֶּ֨לֶךְ֙ הַחַ֔דְרָה וְהַמֶּ֖לֶךְ זָקֵ֣ן מְאֹ֑ד וַֽאֲבִישַׁג֙ הַשּׁ֣וּנַמִּ֔ית מְשָׁרַ֖ת אֶת הַמֶּֽלֶךְ

verses.restored: Bathsheba bowed and prostrated herself before the king. The king said, What is yours/what do you seek?

familiar.text: And Bathsheba bowed, and did obeisance unto the king. And the king said, What wouldest thou?

modern.text: And Bathsheba bowed down in homage to the king, who asked, “What is your desire?”

original.text: וַתִּקֹּ֣ד בַּת שֶׁ֔בַע וַתִּשְׁתַּ֖חוּ לַמֶּ֑לֶךְ וַיֹּ֥אמֶר הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ מַה לָּֽךְ

verses.restored: She said, My lord, you swore by YHWH your Divine to your maidservant: Solomon your son shall reign after me and sit upon my throne.

familiar.text: And she said unto him, My lord, thou swarest by the LORD thy God unto thine handmaid, saying, Assuredly Solomon thy son shall reign after me, and he shall sit upon my throne.

modern.text: “My lord,” she replied, “you yourself swore to your maidservant by the LORD your God: ‘Surely your son Solomon will reign after me, and he will sit on my throne.’

original.text: וַתֹּ֣אמֶר ל֗וֹ אֲדֹנִי֙ אַתָּ֨ה נִשְׁבַּ֜עְתָּ בַּֽיהוָ֤ה אֱלֹהֶ֨יךָ֙ לַֽאֲמָתֶ֔ךָ כִּֽי שְׁלֹמֹ֥ה בְנֵ֖ךְ יִמְלֹ֣ךְ אַחֲרָ֑י וְה֖וּא יֵשֵׁ֥ב עַל כִּסְאִֽי

verses.restored: Now, look, Adonijah has become king, and now, my lord the king, you do not know it.

familiar.text: And now, behold, Adonijah reigneth; and now, my lord the king, thou knowest it not:

modern.text: But now, behold, Adonijah has become king, and you, my lord the king, did not know it.

original.text: וְעַתָּ֕ה הִנֵּ֥ה אֲדֹנִיָּ֖ה מָלָ֑ךְ וְעַתָּ֛ה אֲדֹנִ֥י הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ לֹ֥א יָדָֽעְתָּ

verses.restored: He sacrificed cattle, fattened animals, and sheep in abundance, and invited all sons of the king, Abiathar the priest, and Joab commander of army, but Solomon your servant he did not invite.

familiar.text: And he hath slain oxen and fat cattle and sheep in abundance, and hath called all the sons of the king, and Abiathar the priest, and Joab the captain of the host: but Solomon thy servant hath he not called.

modern.text: And he has sacrificed an abundance of oxen, fattened calves, and sheep, and has invited all the other sons of the king, as well as Abiathar the priest and Joab the commander of the army. But he did not invite your servant Solomon.

original.text: וַ֠יִּזְבַּח שׁ֥וֹר וּֽמְרִיא וְצֹאן֮ לָרֹב֒ וַיִּקְרָא֙ לְכָל בְּנֵ֣י הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ וּלְאֶבְיָתָר֙ הַכֹּהֵ֔ן וּלְיֹאָ֖ב שַׂ֣ר הַצָּבָ֑א וְלִשְׁלֹמֹ֥ה עַבְדְּךָ֖ לֹ֥א קָרָֽא

verses.restored: You, my lord the king—the eyes of all Israel are upon you to tell them who shall sit upon throne of my lord the king after him.

familiar.text: And thou, my lord, O king, the eyes of all Israel are upon thee, that thou shouldest tell them who shall sit on the throne of my lord the king after him.

modern.text: And as for you, my lord the king, the eyes of all Israel are upon you to tell them who will sit on the throne of my lord the king after him.

original.text: וְאַתָּה֙ אֲדֹנִ֣י הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ עֵינֵ֥י כָל יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל עָלֶ֑יךָ לְהַגִּ֣יד לָהֶ֔ם מִ֗י יֵשֵׁ֛ב עַל כִּסֵּ֥א אֲדֹנִֽי הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ אַחֲרָֽיו

verses.restored: Otherwise, when my lord the king lies with his ancestors, I and my son Solomon will be counted offenders.

familiar.text: Otherwise it shall come to pass, when my lord the king shall sleep with his fathers, that I and my son Solomon shall be counted offenders.

modern.text: Otherwise, when my lord the king rests with his fathers, I and my son Solomon will be counted as criminals.”

original.text: וְהָיָ֕ה כִּשְׁכַ֥ב אֲדֹנִֽי הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ עִם אֲבֹתָ֑יו וְהָיִ֗יתִי אֲנִ֛י וּבְנִ֥י שְׁלֹמֹ֖ה חַטָּאִֽים

verses.restored: Look, while she was still speaking with the king, Nathan the prophet came.

familiar.text: And, lo, while she yet talked with the king, Nathan the prophet also came in.

modern.text: And just then, while Bathsheba was still speaking with the king, Nathan the prophet arrived.

original.text: וְהִנֵּ֛ה עוֹדֶ֥נָּה מְדַבֶּ֖רֶת עִם הַמֶּ֑לֶךְ וְנָתָ֥ן הַנָּבִ֖יא בָּֽא

verses.restored: They told the king, Look, Nathan the prophet. He came before the king and bowed on his face to ground.

familiar.text: And they told the king, saying, Behold Nathan the prophet. And when he was come in before the king, he bowed himself before the king with his face to the ground.

modern.text: So the king was told, “Nathan the prophet is here.” And Nathan went in and bowed facedown before the king.

original.text: וַיַּגִּ֤ידוּ לַמֶּ֨לֶךְ֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר הִנֵּ֖ה נָתָ֣ן הַנָּבִ֑יא וַיָּבֹא֙ לִפְנֵ֣י הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ וַיִּשְׁתַּ֧חוּ לַמֶּ֛לֶךְ עַל אַפָּ֖יו אָֽרְצָה

verses.restored: Nathan said, My lord the king, did you say, Adonijah shall reign after me and sit upon my throne?

familiar.text: And Nathan said, My lord, O king, hast thou said, Adonijah shall reign after me, and he shall sit upon my throne?

modern.text: “My lord the king,” said Nathan, “did you say, ‘Adonijah will reign after me, and he will sit on my throne’?

original.text: וַיֹּאמֶר֮ נָתָן֒ אֲדֹנִ֣י הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ אַתָּ֣ה אָמַ֔רְתָּ אֲדֹנִיָּ֖הוּ יִמְלֹ֣ךְ אַחֲרָ֑י וְה֖וּא יֵשֵׁ֥ב עַל כִּסְאִֽי

verses.restored: For he went down this day and sacrificed cattle, fattened animals, and sheep in abundance. He invited all sons of the king, commanders of army, and Abiathar the priest. Look, they eat and drink before him and say, Long live King Adonijah.

familiar.text: For he is gone down this day, and hath slain oxen and fat cattle and sheep in abundance, and hath called all the king’s sons, and the captains of the host, and Abiathar the priest; and, behold, they eat and drink before him, and say, God save king Adonijah.

modern.text: For today he has gone down and sacrificed an abundance of oxen, fattened calves, and sheep, and has invited all the sons of the king, the commanders of the army, and Abiathar the priest. And behold, they are eating and drinking before him, saying, ‘Long live King Adonijah!’

original.text: וְגַם כָּ֖כָה אָמַ֣ר הַמֶּ֑לֶךְ בָּר֨וּךְ יְהוָ֜ה אֱלֹהֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל אֲשֶׁ֨ר נָתַ֥ן הַיּ֛וֹם יֹשֵׁ֥ב עַל כִּסְאִ֖י וְעֵינַ֥י רֹאֽוֹת

verses.restored: All guests who were with Adonijah trembled, arose, and each went his way.

familiar.text: And all the guests that were with Adonijah were afraid, and rose up, and went every man his way.

modern.text: At this, all the guests of Adonijah arose in terror and scattered.

original.text: וַיֶּֽחֶרְדוּ֙ וַיָּקֻ֔מוּ כָּל הַ֨קְּרֻאִ֔ים אֲשֶׁ֖ר לַאֲדֹנִיָּ֑הוּ וַיֵּלְכ֖וּ אִ֥ישׁ לְדַרְכּֽוֹ

verses.restored: Adonijah feared Solomon, arose, went, and grasped horns of altar.

familiar.text: And Adonijah feared because of Solomon, and arose, and went, and caught hold on the horns of the altar.

modern.text: But Adonijah, in fear of Solomon, got up and went to take hold of the horns of the altar.

original.text: וַאֲדֹ֣נִיָּ֔הוּ יָרֵ֖א מִפְּנֵ֣י שְׁלֹמֹ֑ה וַיָּ֣קָם וַיֵּ֔לֶךְ וַֽיַּחֲזֵ֖ק בְּקַרְנ֥וֹת הַמִּזְבֵּֽחַ

verses.restored: It was told Solomon: Look, Adonijah fears King Solomon and has grasped horns of altar, saying, Let King Solomon swear to me this day that he will not kill his servant with sword.

familiar.text: And it was told Solomon, saying, Behold, Adonijah feareth king Solomon: for, lo, he hath caught hold on the horns of the altar, saying, Let king Solomon swear unto me today that he will not slay his servant with the sword.

modern.text: It was reported to Solomon: “Behold, Adonijah fears King Solomon, and he has taken hold of the horns of the altar, saying, ‘Let King Solomon first swear to me not to put his servant to the sword.’”

original.text: וַיֻּגַּ֤ד לִשְׁלֹמֹה֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר הִנֵּה֙ אֲדֹ֣נִיָּ֔הוּ יָרֵ֖א אֶת הַמֶּ֣לֶךְ שְׁלֹמֹ֑ה וְ֠הִנֵּה אָחַ֞ז בְּקַרְנ֤וֹת הַמִּזְבֵּ֨חַ֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר יִשָּֽׁבַֽע לִ֤י כַיּוֹם֙ הַמֶּ֣לֶךְ שְׁלֹמֹ֔ה אִם יָמִ֥ית אֶת עַבְדּ֖וֹ בֶּחָֽרֶב

verses.restored: Solomon said, If he becomes a worthy man, not one hair of him shall fall to earth; but if evil is found in him, he shall die.

familiar.text: And Solomon said, If he will shew himself a worthy man, there shall not an hair of him fall to the earth: but if wickedness shall be found in him, he shall die.

modern.text: And Solomon replied, “If he is a man of character, not a single hair of his will fall to the ground. But if evil is found in him, he will die.”

original.text: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר שְׁלֹמֹ֔ה אִ֚ם יִהְיֶ֣ה לְבֶן חַ֔יִל לֹֽא יִפֹּ֥ל מִשַּׂעֲרָת֖וֹ אָ֑רְצָה וְאִם רָעָ֥ה תִמָּצֵא ב֖וֹ וָמֵֽת

verses.restored: King Solomon sent, and they brought him down from altar. He came and bowed to King Solomon, and Solomon said to him, Go to your house.

familiar.text: So king Solomon sent, and they brought him down from the altar. And he came and bowed himself to king Solomon: and Solomon said unto him, Go to thine house.

modern.text: So King Solomon summoned Adonijah down from the altar, and he came and bowed down before King Solomon, who said to him, “Go to your home.”

original.text: וַיִּשְׁלַ֞ח הַמֶּ֣לֶךְ שְׁלֹמֹ֗ה וַיֹּרִדֻ֨הוּ֙ מֵעַ֣ל הַמִּזְבֵּ֔חַ וַיָּבֹ֕א וַיִּשְׁתַּ֖חוּ לַמֶּ֣לֶךְ שְׁלֹמֹ֑ה וַיֹּֽאמֶר ל֥וֹ שְׁלֹמֹ֖ה לֵ֥ךְ לְבֵיתֶֽךָ

translation_notes: Abishag is a young woman selected across the kingdom for intimate elder care. The text records that David did not have sex with her, but it does not record her consent to recruitment, transport, bodily proximity, or service.
David's aging, inability to stay warm, and dependence do not diminish his human worth. Elder care must center consent, dignity, medical assessment, and the worker's safety.
Bathsheba and Solomon face credible lethal risk in a contested succession. Her coordinated testimony with Nathan occurs under survival pressure.
Adonijah's appearance, birth order, entourage, sacrifices, and elite supporters do not establish a right to rule.
Public acclamation and prophetic-priestly anointing do not make Solomon morally infallible or exempt him from later accountability.
The altar functions as claimed sanctuary, but Solomon's promise remains conditional and vague. Sacred space requires transparent protection, not discretionary royal mercy.
Women, servants, runners, animal handlers, musicians, guards, and residents absorb the labor and danger of elite succession but receive little narrative voice.
safety_note: Do not use this chapter to endorse sexualized caregiving, forced service by young women, dynastic entitlement, secret succession, leader worship, or discretionary execution. Abishag and Bathsheba are persons navigating royal systems, not instruments for male legitimacy.
